subject: how to change or remove background and gridlines from a figure

messages.author: 9e9ea8c0d73c4cac
messages.subject: how to change or remove background and gridlines from a figure
parts:
Dear users,

I've used ggplot(..) and stat_density2d to produce the attached figure. However, I am curious about whether we could remove the grey background and white gridlines from the figure?? 

Appreciate your time and help!

Regards,

Xujun

messages.author: 9c9b5f9c6aaa025d
messages.subject: Re: how to change or remove background and gridlines from a figure
parts:
Play with the `theme` options, e.g.,

theme( line             = element_blank(),
axis.title       = element_blank(), 
axis.text        = element_blank(),
panel.background = element_blank())

messages.author: 000f86f35e1dd157
messages.subject: Re: how to change or remove background and gridlines from a figure
parts:
I assume that your current graph is p
To remove the grey background use:
p+theme_bw()

You can make the white lines invisible but they will still take some space by using the following (source: Wicklam, 2009, Elegant Graphics for Data Analysis)
p + opts(panel.grid.minor = theme_blank())
p + opts(panel.grid.major = theme_blank())
p + opts(panel.background = theme_blank())
p +
opts(axis.title.x = theme_blank(),
axis.title.y = theme_blank())
p + opts(axis.line = theme_segment())

Hope this will help
